date_note: Dailysecu (20 Nov) says the ministry announced the plan on 19 November; the amendment enters pre-legislative notice on 20 November.
title: South Korea plans higher minimum penalty for civil servants who leak personal information
impact: Proposed rule change; not yet in force.
summary: Dailysecu reports South Korea's Ministry of Personnel Management announced on 19 November an amendment to the civil servant disciplinary rules. It would raise the minimum penalty for leaking secrets or personal information from reprimand to pay reduction and let supervisors and non-political agency heads be held accountable for neglecting information-protection oversight. Pre-legislative notice starts 20 November; no effective date is stated.
plain: South Korea proposes tougher minimum discipline, a pay cut, for civil servants who leak personal data, and for bosses who neglect oversight.
exec: Public-sector data leaks in Korea may carry heavier discipline, including for agency heads, once the rule takes effect.

validation.note: One Dailysecu article read in full; the ministry's own notice was not read.
